card.keepWhy: The stone you dread may already be moved.
sources: Mark 16:1-4 (when the sabbath was past, Mary Magdalen, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought sweet spices to anoint him; very early on the first day of the week they come to the sepulchre; “Who shall roll us back the stone from the door of the sepulchre?”; looking, they saw the stone rolled back, for it was very great). Douay-Rheims.

Luke 24:1-11 (two men in shining apparel; “Why seek you the living with the dead? He is not here, but is risen”; the women, Mary Magdalen, Joanna and Mary of James, told these things to the apostles; “these words seemed to them as idle tales; and they did not believe them”). Also Matthew 28:1-8; John 20:1-18.

Catechism of the Catholic Church 638-641 (the resurrection; Mary Magdalene and the holy women the first messengers of the Resurrection, even to the apostles). Thomas Aquinas, Commentary on John 20 (apostolorum apostola); Congregation for Divine Worship, decree of 3 June 2016 raising her memorial to a feast.

General Norms for the Liturgical Year and the Calendar 22 (the fifty days from Easter Sunday to Pentecost celebrated as one feast). Spanish Pascua, Italian Pasqua, from Greek/Latin Pascha, Hebrew Pesach.
check: The telling blends Mark (the worry about the stone) and Luke (the two men, “why look for the living among the dead”, the apostles’ disbelief); the source line says “from the Gospels”. Confirm.

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? is there something ahead of you this week that feels too heavy to move?
options: i’m sorry. hold it while you watch. these women had one too.
small stones are still heavy. watch this.
then keep this story for the day you do.

steps.line: Very early on Sunday morning, after Jesus was buried, a few women walked to his tomb with spices, to care for his body. The apostles were not with them.
On the way, they worried. A huge stone sealed the tomb. “Who will roll the stone away for us?” They went anyway.

steps.q: They reach the tomb with no plan for the stone. What do they find?
o: Roman guards who turn them away
The stone too heavy, so they wait
steps.why: Mark adds that the stone was “very great.” Matthew says an angel rolled it away; Mark and Luke just say it was done before they arrived.

steps.line: When they arrived, the stone was already rolled back. The tomb was empty.
Two men in dazzling clothes stood beside them. “Why do you look for the living among the dead? He is not here. He has risen.”

steps.q: The two men tell the women to remember something. What?
o: What Jesus had told them in Galilee
The psalms they sang at Passover
steps.why: Luke says the men reminded them Jesus had said he’d be handed over, crucified, and rise on the third day. “And they remembered his words.”

steps.line: The women ran to tell the apostles. The men didn’t believe them at first. It sounded like nonsense.

steps.q: All four Gospels say women were the first at the empty tomb. Why does that detail stand out?
o: The men had already left for Galilee
A woman’s word counted for less then
steps.why: Many scholars note it would be an odd detail to invent. Tradition calls Mary Magdalene the apostle to the apostles; since 2016 her day is a feast.

steps.line: Today, Easter isn’t one day. Catholics keep it for fifty days, longer than Lent. And every Sunday keeps a little of that morning.
steps.label: today

steps.q: Easter is Pascua in Spanish and Pasqua in Italian. Where does that name come from?
o: Pax, the Latin word for peace
steps.why: Jesus died and rose at Passover time, so many languages name Easter after Pesach. English and German are among the exceptions, along with several Slavic languages.

say: here’s what i love. the women walked toward the stone with no plan, just love. and it was already moved.
catholics believe the resurrection is the center of everything: jesus truly rose, and death doesn’t get the last word. that’s why easter lasts fifty days, and every sunday is a small easter.

steps.q: The women brought spices to care for a dead body. What does that tell you about what they expected?
o: They knew he would rise that morning
They expected a body, not an empty tomb
They wanted to move him somewhere safer
steps.why: You don’t bring burial spices for someone you expect to see alive. Many readers find their surprise is part of why the story rings true.

today.say: think of the stone you named. today, take one small step toward it, without a plan, the way the women did: a call, an email, a first page. if you pray, you can bring it to God on the way.
options: good. you might find it already moved.
that’s a step too. the women started by walking.
